newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Geomancer okays Tung's new Hong Kong headquarters.
newsitem.headline: Geomancer okays Tung's new Hong Kong headquarters.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa can rest easy when he finally moves into his plush new offices -- or so said a fung shui master, an expert in the art of Chinese geomancy.

Overlooking a waterfall and the future Chinese foreign ministry building, the 600 square metre (yard) office in the Central business district was cleared by the expert who was called in to inspect the site on Tuesday.

"Fung Shui is important for the Chinese and we have a saying that even if you don't believe it, there's no harm in doing it," said Fanny Law, a senior civil servant seconded by the Hong Kong government to be Tung's private secretary.
"Fung Shui", literally wind and water, is an age-old philosophy on ensuring natural harmony among the elements which many Chinese regard as a guarantee to good fortune and hedge against bad luck.

Shipping tycoon Tung, who will step into Governor Chris Patten's shoes when British rule ends at midnight on June 30, said last year he did not want to move into the Governor's official residence because of bad fung shui.
Tung and his team are expected to move into the new office after Chinese New Year which falls in the first week of February.
The office is expected to cost taxpayers HK$500,000 ($64,600) a month, experts said.
